items.title: Chester Zardis Interview, 1970-02-14
items.q: He said, well, I'm going out to Bubba Luce. He was staying in the club. He'd go out there and get forty, fifty dollars from the man all the time.

ctx.x: You take, you know, like that neighborhood up there now, you know, up around Barcaloosa and all, I mean, I don't know how you feel, but I wouldn't like to go out there too much.

No. Well, it wasn't like that at that time. Everybody didn't know their place, you know what I mean? You go in your place, and they go in their place, and that's the way they got along like that. It wasn't no humbug at all out there, because the white people were just as, you know, glad to have the colored band to play for them, and to have the white band, which they didn't have no white band out there at that time, you know? And that's why they used to catch Buddy all the time. And when we'd be waiting for the…
How much would you get paid for a job then?
